newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria plans tender for second GSM operator.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria plans tender for second GSM operator.

text.p: The Bulgarian Post and Communication Committee (BPCC), keen to get a good price in the planned sale of a stake in its telecom company, said on Thursday it was preparing a tender for a second GSM operator.

BPCC deputy chairman Simeon Tsenov said the committee would prepare its proposal for announcing the tender within three months as it had to coordinate with other ministries, including the environmental authorities.
"Then the government will discuss and take a decision on launching the tender," Tsenov told Reuters.
BPCC chairman Lyubomir Kolarov has said the price for the 25 percent stake in Bulgarian Telecommunication Company (BTC) would be higher if the company was also a GSM operator.
Tsenov said the BPCC planned to invite foreign bidders with experience in the telecom sector to consult with the committee in preparing the GSM tender and contract.
He said the defence ministry had already arranged two frequencies for the GSM. Telecom authorities have said a second licence would promote competition.
Last year two BTC joint ventures expressed interest in operating GSM. They are Bulfon, a venture with Greek group Intracom, and Mobikom, a venture with Britain's Cable and Wireless Plc.
Cable and Wireless, which has 49 percent of Mobikom, has also said it would be interested in bidding for a GSM operator.
Mobikom, set up in 1992, is building up Bulgaria's major mobile cellular telephone system and plans to cover some 65 percent of the population by the year-end.
South Korea's giant Daewoo Corp said earlier this month it was interested in participating in a tender for a GSM operator.

Bulgaria's existing GSM operator Mobiltel is seeking to sell its licence. Mobiltel is a joint venture set up by one of Bulgaria's major private financial groups Tron and was granted the GSM licence two years ago.
